clue.text: The last day for shaping mahogany?

indicators.note: shaping the wood means working its letters into a new form, so the word mahogany is rearranged

explanation.surface: A carpenter's question about the final day set aside for working a piece of mahogany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for shaping' tells you to rearrange the eight letters of MAHOGANY. The Scottish New Year's Eve celebration is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the celebration on 31 December, the final day of the year, carries this name.

clue.text: Ancient old boy alone, note!

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school
sole means alone, the only one
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An exclamation drawing attention to a very old former pupil who is on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date and no longer in use can be called ancient in the loose sense of very old.

clue.text: As writer of various essays, Scillies man comes out on time

indicators.note: coming out suggests emerging in a different form, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from the Isles of Scilly turns up punctually, described as an essayist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out' rearranges SCILLIES MAN; 'on time' adds T at the end. The Isles of Scilly lie off Cornwall in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A compiler or author of assorted pieces on mixed topics is a miscellany writer, an essayist of many subjects.

clue.text: Two, for example, can knock one senseless

definitions.meaning: two is an instance of a figure or integer
read as ..., a thing that makes one numb or without feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Two is an example of a figure, and something that deadens feeling could jokingly be a 'numb-er'.

clue.text: Year ago, retired for meditation

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word ago is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone gave up a calming practice twelve months back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' is the reversal signal: a word that has retired has drawn back, so it reads right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu discipline of posture and breathing is widely practised as a form of contemplation.

clue.text: Former member of the house…

parts.note: reads like an ex-MP of the House of Commons, but means an earlier member of a family line, a house in the sense of dynasty

explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is an earlier member of a family, and a noble family is called a house.

clue.text: … house in home counties, next to motorway

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East, abbreviated SE
the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, written here as MI

explanation.surface: A dwelling located in the counties around London, beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London; the motorway is the M1, with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour, is commonly shortened to this.

clue.text: Time to support guide providing cheapest accommodation on board

indicators.note: in a down clue one word supports another by sitting below it, so the time word comes after

parts.note: to steer is to guide or direct
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone needs time to back up a tour guide offering the most budget berths on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to support' puts AGE beneath STEER.
explanation.definitionFit: On old passenger ships the lowest-fare section, near the rudder gear, was the poorest class of travel.

clue.text: Decoration of books with gold title at front

indicators.note: says the gold and title pieces stand at the front, before the books

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a name is a title or designation
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A book embellished with a gilded title on its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldic gold; NT, the New Testament, is a common crossword stand-in for 'books'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adornment or trinket is something added purely to embellish.

clue.text: Fertility goddess currently in Oxford?

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian mother goddess of fertility and magic
currently is a pun on a river current: the stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford has its own name

explanation.definitionFit: She is the Egyptian goddess of motherhood, and the Thames at Oxford goes by the same name.

clue.text: Savoy, for example, immaculate for the summer visitor

parts.note: the Savoy is a variety of crinkly-leaved cabbage
immaculate means spotless, pure white

explanation.surface: Sounds like praise of a spotless London hotel being perfect for holiday guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Savoy' suggests the London hotel, with 'summer visitor' a holiday guest; in fact it is a cabbage variety and the visitor a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: This butterfly appears in gardens during the warm months and lays its eggs on brassicas.

clue.text: Competence up?

parts.note: up here means mounted on a horse, so the skill is that of a rider in the saddle

explanation.definitionFit: Skill at riding, being able to handle oneself when mounted, is an equestrian competence.

clue.text: Spring roll, say, from good stock

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than read, a soundalike

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A bakery's spring roll is supposedly made with good ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring roll' looks like the Chinese snack but splits in two; 'say' makes BREAD into its soundalike BRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone descended from a respectable family line, with good breeding, is so described.

clue.text: Composer of a spirited French trio?

definitions.text: Composer of a spirited French trio?

parts.words: Composer of a spirited French trio?
parts.note: composer suggests music, but it means the writer of a novel about three dashing French swordsmen

explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist wrote The Three Musketeers, about a lively band of three soldiers.

clue.text: Greedy fish, given new head, would be capital!

indicators.note: a new head means the first letter of the fish is swapped for another

parts.note: the pirana, a variant spelling of piranha, is a voracious fish

explanation.surface: A voracious fish with a fresh head would be splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: PIRANA is an accepted spelling of piranha; changing its first letter P to T gives the city. 'capital!' also poses as an old exclamation meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Albania.

clue.text: For hill shaped like this, take me to South America

explanation.surface: Travel advice for reaching a peculiarly shaped hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish word for table also names a flat-topped hill, which the clue's 'like this' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped elevation with steep sides, common in the American south-west, is named from the Spanish for table.

clue.text: Instruments of African wood-tappers

parts.note: wood-tappers suggests woodpeckers, but these are players striking wooden bars with mallets, an instrument of African origin

explanation.definitionFit: These xylophone-like percussion instruments with wooden keys came originally from Africa.

clue.text: Longest support for a walker?

parts.note: support for a walker suggests a stick or frame, but means the body's longest bone, in the thigh

explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone is the longest bone in the human body and bears weight in walking.

clue.text: Resolution of company head

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: The decision made by a business's chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, found in place names like Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve and steadiness of purpose are the same quality of determination.

clue.text: Relief from sea-serpents

indicators.note: from tells you the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Respite from the monsters of the deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside SEA-SERPENTS, between the first S and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort or alleviation of pain or worry is freedom from discomfort.

clue.text: Beach-jumper?

parts.note: a jumper could be a sweater, but here it is a small leaping crustacean living on the shore

explanation.definitionFit: This small hopping crustacean lives in seaside sand and leaps about like an insect.

clue.text: Constable, say, approaching mole with a sword

parts.note: the painter John Constable was a Royal Academician, RA
a mole is a stone breakwater, which a pier resembles

explanation.surface: A police constable closing in on a burrowing animal while armed with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' is not a police officer but the painter, a member of the Royal Academy (RA); 'mole' is not the animal but a harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, light, two-edged blade used for thrusting is a duelling weapon.

clue.text: Suffers us to carry blemishes outside

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside, so the stain word holds the other piece
the blemishes word goes around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: stains are marks or blemishes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody tolerates our bearing marks on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' and 'outside' together make one container signal: the blemishes enclose the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo or experience an injury or loss is to bear it, as in sustaining damage.

clue.text: Wicked, almost entirely, after Sunday

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the Sunday letter
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: in full means completely, entirely

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's verdict that nearly everything after Sunday is immoral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last L from IN FULL to leave INFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral, transgressing religious law, is what wicked conduct is.

clue.text: Silent monkey, jumping about in new town

indicators.note: jumping about suggests the letters leap into a new order

explanation.surface: A quiet monkey bouncing around somewhere in a planned town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping about' rearranges SILENT MONKEY. The town is a post-war planned settlement in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Buckinghamshire settlement was designated in 1967 under Britain's programme of planned communities.

clue.text: Cobbler works at one to stand up

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker shapes footwear on a foot-shaped block
to stand up means to endure or hold out

explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker's foot-shaped block bears this name, and to endure or keep going is the same verb.

clue.text: Nose resection takes ages

indicators.note: a resection is surgical cutting and rearranging, so the letters of nose are reordered

explanation.surface: An operation on the nose takes a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Very long periods of time, often in the plural, are spoken of as aeons.

clue.text: Headlight of type that can not go wrong

definitions.text: Headlight of type that can not go wrong

parts.words: Headlight of type that can not go wrong
parts.note: headlight is not a car lamp but a light around the head, worn in pictures by a saint, a person who cannot sin

explanation.definitionFit: The ring of light painted round a saint's head marks holiness.

clue.text: One makes a killing with a pair of donkeys, past the post?

indicators.note: a pair means the donkey word appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
a horse past the winning post is in, home

explanation.surface: A racegoer wins big with two donkeys finishing the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a killing' sounds like winning big on the races; it means committing murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially a hired one, literally carries out a killing.

clue.text: A Shropshire Lad"?

parts.note: the title of Housman's poems suggests itself, but the clue just asks for a native of the county, whose old name is Salop

explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the old name for the English county, so a person from there takes this demonym.
